h1: Cloakroom & WC installation in Stoke Poges

hero.intro: Stoke Poges houses tend to be large, which usually means a downstairs cloakroom gets added for convenience rather than necessity — a second WC off a boot room, utility corridor or hallway in a house that's already generous on space. We fit the WC and basin into whatever compact footprint you've identified; you buy the sanitaryware, tiles and brassware, we handle the rest.

sections.heading: Why a cloakroom makes sense in Stoke Poges's larger houses
sections.body: Stoke Poges is a village of large plots and substantial houses, with Stoke Park's golf and country club giving the area its best-known identity. The housing ranges from older period detached homes to more recent executive-style builds, many set well back from the road on sizeable gardens. In a house of that scale, a single family bathroom upstairs often isn't enough once children, guests or staff are regularly in and out of the ground floor, and a cloakroom is the practical answer — far cheaper and less disruptive than adding another full bathroom. Because these properties generally give us more room to manoeuvre on layout than a smaller terraced house would, finding a workable location for the new WC and routing a waste run to it rarely runs into the structural constraints that would stop the same project in a tighter home.

sections.heading: Where cloakrooms typically go in a house this size
sections.body: In the larger Stoke Poges properties we work on, a cloakroom conversion usually lands in one of a handful of spots: a redundant understairs cupboard, a corner carved out of an oversized utility or boot room, or a seldom-used store off the main hallway. Each of these comes with its own constraints — an under-stairs space usually has a sloped ceiling that dictates where the cistern and any shelving sit, while a utility-room corner is more likely to have a square profile but needs stud walls built to separate it off properly, with sound and damp considered since it's adjoining a wet space. Whichever location you're considering, the fittings themselves are chosen for the footprint: a wall-hung WC with a concealed cistern, and a corner or slimline basin rather than anything with a pedestal, so the finished room doesn't feel like a compromise.

sections.heading: How we run the installation
sections.body: We begin with a £125 survey to measure the chosen space precisely, locate the nearest waste and water supply, and agree a final layout before you order any sanitaryware. On installation day, we strip out whatever's currently occupying the space — cupboard carcasses, old shelving, redundant pipework — then first-fix the new plumbing and electrics, build out any stud walls and tile, and fit and connect the WC, basin and extractor before a full snag. Fit-only installs start from £3,500, with the final figure depending on how much new waste and water routing is needed and whether stud walls have to be built from scratch, which is more common in a boot-room or utility conversion than in an existing under-stairs void.

sections.heading: Book your survey
sections.body: If you've identified a potential cloakroom location in your Stoke Poges home — whether that's under the stairs, off a boot room or carved from a utility space — call or WhatsApp 07399 651836 to arrange the £125 survey and get a firm quote.

faqs.q: Can you build a new stud wall to create a cloakroom from a utility room?
faqs.a: Yes — this is common in larger Stoke Poges houses where a utility or boot room has spare floor area. We build the partition, first-fix the plumbing and electrics, then tile and fit as part of the same project.

faqs.q: Do you supply the WC and basin for a Stoke Poges cloakroom?
faqs.a: No — we're fit-only. You source the sanitaryware, brassware and tiles, and we carry out the strip-out, first fix, tiling, plumbing and snagging.

faqs.q: Will the large plot size make the installation easier?
faqs.a: It generally gives us more flexibility on where to route a new waste run than a terraced property would, since there's less structural constraint to work around. The exact layout is confirmed at survey.

faqs.q: What does a cloakroom installation cost in Stoke Poges?
faqs.a: Fit-only installs start from £3,500. The final price depends on whether a stud wall needs building, how far the new waste run has to travel, and the fittings you've specified.
